comparator.name: International Bachelor in Psychology
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 ESSB EER Appendix D pages40–41 establishes the revised post-2023 curriculum:60EC each year, one consistent specialisation and25EC regulated choice space. The public overview uses some different labels (Human Learning; Memory), so formal names and weights control. Test-subject hours are a separate compulsory non-credit obligation. Articles3.6,4.1–4.3,7.4 and AppendixB govern choices, progression, participation and completion. Brain & Cognition is retained through the official-order tie-break, not a claim that neuroscience is the least specialised form of psychology.

alternatives.label: Closest match to Psychology
alternatives.concept: Social, developmental, clinical and cognitive psychology form the core, supported by quantitative and qualitative research, evidence synthesis, organisational psychology and behavioural decision-making. Sociology examines the social institutions and cultural contexts in which behaviour occurs.
progression: Research Methods & Statistics begins in Semester 2 before multivariate statistics and advanced research. Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes the clinical, developmental and cognitive courses requiring it. Sociology progresses from introduction through modern theory to contemporary civil-society research. Epidemiology supplies specific population-health evidence; leadership and behavioural economics supply applied settings for psychological decisions.

alternatives.label: Brain & cognition
alternatives.concept: Neurobiology, perception, higher cognitive functions and language are studied alongside psychological development, mental health and assessment. Statistics, research synthesis, data science, machine learning and computer vision support empirical inquiry; cell biology, physiology and laboratory work provide complementary biological methods.
alternatives.distinctness: Cognitive/neural science, cellular and physiological foundations, experimental laboratory and computational data methods replace part of the social, ethical and organisational mix.
progression: Brain/behaviour and life-science gateways precede their formal continuations. Data science precedes machine learning; foundational statistics precedes R-based systematic review and meta-analysis. Cellular biology, physiology and biochemical laboratory work complement neuroscience without substituting for psychological assessment or specialist brain-imaging training.

alternatives.label: Psychology, leadership & organisations
alternatives.concept: Organisational psychology, motivation, leadership, diversity, negotiation and workplace health are connected to social and cognitive psychology, behavioural economics and applied research. Sociology examines organisations in their wider social setting; entrepreneurship and AI-related business study provide specific settings for organisational decisions. Higher cognitive functions develops experimental understanding of attention, emotion and decision-making.
alternatives.labelReason: The broader label reflects the completed mix of psychology, leadership, organisations, sociology, communication, business and behavioural economics.
alternatives.distinctness: Organisational motivation, leadership, diversity, negotiation and applied market research replace the neuroscience/biological emphasis.
progression: The business gateway precedes applied market research, and statistics precedes organisational psychology and negotiation. Psychology and sociology foundations precede their formal continuations. Advanced applied courses may precede other advisory foundations where the open curriculum permits this; no unstated hard prerequisite is introduced.

routeSelection.basis: The generic target does not select a specialisation. None of four substantive specialisations is established as broadly representative or least specialised. Brain & Cognition is the first specialisation encountered in the current formal curriculum, in the Bachelor-2 table on page40; use that neutral order, independently of UCR fit. The different order in the subsequent Bachelor-3 table does not override the first complete-pathway occurrence.

selection.assessment: Three substantive responses survive the source-content challenge. The closest has broad psychology as its organising subject; brain/cognition has four cognition courses plus psychological inquiry and specific biological/computational methods; the organisational option has organisational behaviour, leadership and behavioural research. Clinical and educational directions are evidenced but no fourth programme is authorised by the maximum-three rule. None reproduces Erasmus professional practicals, test theory or required thesis.

blocks: Partial subject relationship through sensory processing and action; different course size and practical requirements remain.
Language processing and its psychological/neurobiological mechanisms overlap; the UCR course is not a complete substitute for memory and language.
No single UCR course is established as reproducing this particular practical; UCR research and synthesis courses retain their separate scopes.
The UCR research seminar uses R for systematic reviews and meta-analysis. This is a specific partial data-analysis relationship; it does not reproduce the Erasmus practical.

UCR offers research-method and evidence-synthesis courses, but no single canonical UCR course substantially reproduces the comparator practical in intervention research without overstating partial overlap.
Both concern development, but their distinct content is insufficiently established for a direct correspondence.

notes.text: Erasmus includes a dedicated psychometrics sequence, psychodiagnostic and communication practicals, a 14-EC thesis and a formal specialisation. UCR offers substantial psychology, cognitive-science and organisational study, including psychological assessment concepts and R-based research synthesis, but does not reproduce those specialist practicals or the same disciplinary degree. Becoming a clinical psychologist requires further qualifications; neither bachelor alone provides professional registration.

audience.programmeDescription: The English-taught International Bachelor in Psychology at Erasmus University Rotterdam studies behaviour, thought, emotion and development through psychological theory, empirical research and statistics. Students complete practical training, choose one of four specialisations and write a bachelor thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options pursue broad psychology, brain and cognition, or psychology in organisations. Each has substantial psychological content and empirical methods, with different complementary study. Shared rows indicate specific partial subject or method relationships. Blank cells preserve gaps in specialist training, and none of these programmes guarantees admission to a psychology master or professional qualification.

curriculum.routeLabel: Brain & Cognition; approved minor and psychology electives
curriculum.limitation: One permitted specialisation is shown. The minor needs programme approval; the two psychology electives come from the programme’s restricted offer. Test-subject participation is also compulsory and carries no EC. Year 2 requires positive binding study advice; Year 3 and specialisation study require Year 1 completed. Thesis entry requires 135 EC. Tutorial and practical attendance requirements apply.
